column2: Baker presents an objective view of the life of Tiberius Caesar, the second emperor of Rome, and successor to Augustus. While covering the years from age thirteen to the emperor's death, the author considers issues of Augustus' succession, Tiberius' military career, and the challenging political aspects of the early Roman Empire. - Summary by Mark Harrington

Few Americans today realize that Michigan and Wisconsin were once part of French Canada. French influence in the region continued through the eighteenth century, decades after France ceded Canada to Great Britain at the end of the Seven Years’ War in 1763.
My Little Athenian Cousin of Long Ago is about a boy named Hiero growing up in ancient Athens. In the story, he and a boy named Duris grow in friendship while learning about life in the city.

A Strange Love: A Novel of Abnormal Passion was first published in French as Escal-Vigor in 1899, the English translation nine years later. It is as relevant today as it was a century ago, treating the torture of coming out to oneself, the fear and loneliness of isolation, the high cost of coming out to others, and the high value of personal integrity.

The Book of Psalms, or Psalter, was written by King David and various other authors over a period of several hundred years beginning around 1000 BC. It consists of divinely inspired hymn-like poems expressing the heart of lives lived in God's presence.

Count Felix von Luckner, German naval war officer of World War One, through the words of Lowell Thomas, relates his adventures at sea as a young man through his German naval command in Word War I. Von Luckner is best known as the one who broke through the British blockade and disrupted Allied shipping in a windjammer, under sail, while managing to avoid killing any Allied crews.
